title: Interface Control Record
body:
Overview

This record documents Interface Control Record within the Mission Systems Integration Database. Maps interfaces, dependencies, system requirements and integration tests. It gives the archive a reusable, checkable entry for one recurring task: the entry states what the task is, how it is done, and what result was measured or computed when the accompanying demo program ran. The record is written so a reader can follow it without any other document open, and so an AI can apply it to a new task of the same shape without guessing at missing steps. Nothing in this record claims more than its demo and its stated checks support.

How it works

The method in each record is interface-first engineering: every connection between parts of a system is written down as a contract naming the data, the format, the timing, and the error behavior. Integration tests then check each contract directly, and a requirement is only marked satisfied when its test passes. This is support engineering for complex platforms: making parts work together reliably.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this entry is concrete. The demo program that accompanies this record ran at build time and produced a real, checkable result, beginning with: contracts checked: 5. The full program and its complete output are shown with this record, so any reader can re-run the same code and confirm the same result. Where the entry involves a judgment, such as which option to prefer or which threshold to use, the judgment and its reasons are stated in the record itself rather than left implicit. Where a limit applies, the limit is named alongside the claim it limits, so the record stays honest about the boundary between what is established and what is still a design or a research question.

Use and ladder

An integration team uses these records to plan test order, to trace a failure to the contract it broke, and to prove that a change in one part did not silently break another. Teaching ladder: this record is ranked simple. Simple records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records handle the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. Feasibility tier: established. Implementation status: established. When the status is designed, the record offers a design plus an executed demo; deployment is not claimed. Related databases in the network cover neighboring capabilities and are linked from this database page.
demo_code:
# Interface Control Record: check every interface contract and report completeness.
contracts = [('data format', True), ('timing', True), ('error behavior', True), ('versioning', False), ('security boundary', True)]
passed = [name for name, ok in contracts if ok]
failed = [name for name, ok in contracts if not ok]
print("contracts checked:", len(contracts))
print("passed:", len(passed), passed)
print("failed:", len(failed), failed)
print("integration ready:", not failed)
